sources.note: Nothing: the article is a lexicostatistic/sociolinguistic update of Grimes & Grimes 1987; a search of the full scanned text for stress|accent|penult finds no linguistic hit. Silent open source, useful only for identity, speaker numbers and the Baras = Ende equation.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78. Canberra: ANU. (entry 8 'Baras', printed p. 59; Appendix E symbols p. 96; language-abbreviation list p. 19)
sources.note: Nothing for Baras. The Baras entry (p. 59) gives classification, ~4,000 speakers, location, then: 'No other information is currently available.' Baras is not among the Appendix E wordlists (no BRS/Baras code in the p. 19 abbreviation list; the 'BAL baras' line is the Balanipa Mandar word for 'uncooked rice'), so the generic Appendix E note p. 96 ('Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable') is not based on any Baras data.

sources.citation: Valkama, Kari. 1987. UNHAS-SIL sociolinguistic survey: Kabupaten Mamuju. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL South Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys 1983-1987 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 5), 99-117. Ujung Pandang: SIL.
sources.note: Nothing. Baras treated as Kaili dialect no. 3 (pp. 105-106): 'Baras, represented by the Salubiro and Bambaloka wordlists. This dialect is spoken only in a few of the villages of desa Baras, by about 50 households. The elders fear that their language is dying out'. Lexicostatistics only; no phonology, no stress (a full-text search for stress/accent full text for stress/penult/accent: no hits).
